name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q01 - Moles of silver chloride precipitated per mole

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination compounds given in Column I with the moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) precipitated per mole of compound on reaction with excess silver nitrate solution given in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 6NH_{3}}\)i. \(0\text{ mol}\)
B. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 5NH_{3}}\)ii. \(1\text{ mol}\)
C. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 4NH_{3}}\)iii. \(2\text{ mol}\)
D. \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 3NH_{3}}\)iv. \(3\text{ mol}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Werner's formulation of coordination compounds
According to Werner's theory, the groups inside the coordination sphere (enclosed in square brackets) are non-ionisable and bonded by secondary valencies, while groups outside the coordination sphere satisfy primary valencies and ionise in aqueous solution to yield chloride ions that precipitate as \(\mathrm{AgCl}\) on treatment with excess cold \(\mathrm{AgNO_{3}}\) solution.

Step 2: Analysis of the hexammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 6NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]Cl_{3}}\). In aqueous solution, one mole of this complex dissociates into three moles of chloride ions, precipitating \(3\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 3: Analysis of the pentammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 5NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}}\). It possesses two ionisable chloride ions outside the coordination sphere, precipitating \(2\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 4: Analysis of the tetrammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 4NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{4}Cl_{2}]Cl}\). It has one ionisable chloride ion outside the coordination sphere, yielding \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 5: Analysis of the triammine complex
The complex \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 3NH_{3}}\) is formulated as \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{3}Cl_{3}]}\). All three chloride ions reside inside the coordination sphere satisfying secondary valencies; hence no chloride ions ionise in solution, resulting in \(0\text{ mol}\) of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 6NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(3\text{ mol}\), \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 5NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(2\text{ mol}\), \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 4NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(1\text{ mol}\), and \(\mathrm{CoCl_{3}\cdot 3NH_{3}}\) pairs with \(0\text{ mol}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q02 - Coordination polyhedra of common complex entities

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities in Column I with their respective coordination polyhedra (geometrical arrangements) in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\)i. Octahedral
B. \(\mathrm{[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}}\)ii. Trigonal bipyramidal
C. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\)iii. Tetrahedral
D. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\)iv. Square planar

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual definition of coordination polyhedron
The spatial arrangement of the ligand atoms directly attached to the central metal atom or ion defines a coordination polyhedron about the central metal.

Step 2: Geometry of tetracarbonylnickel(0)
Nickel in \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\) has an oxidation state of zero with electronic configuration \(3d^{10}\). The metal centre undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation, giving a tetrahedral coordination polyhedron.

Step 3: Geometry of tetrachloridoplatinate(II)
Platinum(II) in \(\mathrm{[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}}\) is a \(5d^8\) system. Square planar geometry is strongly favoured for \(4d\) and \(5d\) metal ions with \(d^8\) configurations involving \(dsp^2\) hybridisation.

Step 4: Geometry of pentacarbonyliron(0)
Iron in \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\) has zero oxidation state and coordination number 5. Pairing of \(3d\) electrons provides one empty inner \(d\) orbital, leading to \(dsp^3\) hybridisation with a trigonal bipyramidal coordination polyhedron.

Step 5: Geometry of hexaamminecobalt(III)
Cobalt(III) in \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) has coordination number 6. Six ligand donor atoms surround the cobalt ion symmetrically at the vertices of an octahedron, yielding an octahedral coordination polyhedron.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\) corresponds to tetrahedral, \(\mathrm{[PtCl_{4}]^{2-}}\) corresponds to square planar, \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\) corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal, and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) corresponds to octahedral.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q03 - Biological and medicinal coordination compounds and metals

questiontext.text:
Match the biological/medicinal coordination compounds in Column I with the central metal atom/ion present in them in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. Chlorophylli. Cobalt
B. Haemoglobinii. Platinum
C. Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\)iii. Magnesium
D. Cis-platiniv. Iron

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Bio-inorganic roles of coordination complexes
Coordination compounds are vital components of biological systems and have profound applications in medicine. Specific metal ions serve as the active coordination centers in complex biomolecules and pharmaceuticals.

Step 2: Identification of metal in chlorophyll
Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plants responsible for photosynthesis; it is a coordination compound containing magnesium as its central metal.

Step 3: Identification of metal in haemoglobin
Haemoglobin is the red pigment in erythrocytes responsible for oxygen transport; it is a coordination compound containing iron(II) coordinated to a porphyrin ring.

Step 4: Identification of metal in vitamin B12
Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\) (cyanocobalamin), which prevents pernicious anaemia, is a macrocyclic corrin ring coordination complex of cobalt.

Step 5: Identification of metal in cis-platin
Cis-platin, \(\mathrm{\textit{cis}\text{-}[Pt(NH_{3})_{2}Cl_{2}]}\), is an established anti-tumour platinum complex used in cancer chemotherapy.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: Chlorophyll pairs with Magnesium, Haemoglobin pairs with Iron, Vitamin \(\mathrm{B_{12}}\) pairs with Cobalt, and Cis-platin pairs with Platinum.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q04 - Types of structural isomerism in complex pairs

questiontext.text:
Match the pairs of coordination compounds in Column I with the type of isomerism they exhibit in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(NO_{2})]Cl_{2}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(ONO)]Cl_{2}}\)i. Coordination isomerism
B. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Cr(CN)_{6}]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}]}\)ii. Solvate (hydrate) isomerism
C. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(SO_{4})]Br}\) and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}Br]SO_{4}}\)iii. Linkage isomerism
D. \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]Cl_{3}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}\cdot H_{2}O}\)iv. Ionisation isomerism

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of structural isomerism
Structural isomers have the same empirical formula but differ in the arrangement of chemical bonds, distribution of ligands between spheres, or ligand binding mode.

Step 2: Linkage isomerism
Linkage isomerism arises in a coordination compound containing an ambidentate ligand capable of coordinating through two different donor atoms. In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(NO_{2})]Cl_{2}}\), the nitrite ligand binds through nitrogen, whereas in \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(ONO)]Cl_{2}}\), it binds through oxygen. This represents linkage isomerism.

Step 3: Coordination isomerism
Coordination isomerism occurs in compounds composed of both complex cation and complex anion due to the interchange of ligands between the two metal entities. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}][Cr(CN)_{6}]}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(NH_{3})_{6}][Co(CN)_{6}]}\) illustrate coordination isomerism.

Step 4: Ionisation isomerism
Ionisation isomerism arises when a counter ion in a compound displaces a ligand from the coordination sphere, producing different ions in solution. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}(SO_{4})]Br}\) gives bromide ions while \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{5}Br]SO_{4}}\) gives sulphate ions upon dissociation in water. This represents ionisation isomerism.

Step 5: Solvate isomerism
Solvate (hydrate) isomerism differs by whether a solvent molecule (water) is directly bonded to the metal ion as a ligand or merely present as free solvent molecules of crystallisation in the crystal lattice. \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}]Cl_{3}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Cr(H_{2}O)_{5}Cl]Cl_{2}\cdot H_{2}O}\) illustrate solvate isomerism.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: the pair with nitro and nitrito complexes matches linkage isomerism; the hexammine-hexacyanide complex pair matches coordination isomerism; the sulphato-bromido complex pair matches ionisation isomerism; and the hydrated chromium chloride pair matches solvate isomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q05 - Classification and denticity of various ligands

questiontext.text:
Match the ligands given in Column I with their denticity/bonding character described in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\)i. Ambidentate unidentate ligand
B. Ethane-1,2-diamineii. Neutral unidentate ligand
C. \(\mathrm{SCN^{-}}\)iii. Hexadentate chelating ligand
D. \(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\)iv. Didentate chelating ligand

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of ligand denticity
The number of donor atoms through which a ligand binds to a single central metal ion is known as its denticity. Ligands binding through two or more donor sites are polydentate (chelating), whereas those coordinating through one site are unidentate.

Step 2: Denticity of ethylenediaminetetraacetate
Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion (\(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\)) possesses two nitrogen donor atoms and four oxygen donor atoms from acetate groups, allowing it to bind through six donor atoms simultaneously as an important hexadentate chelating ligand.

Step 3: Denticity of ethane-1,2-diamine
Ethane-1,2-diamine (\(\mathrm{H_{2}NCH_{2}CH_{2}NH_{2}}\)) has two nitrogen donor atoms each bearing a lone pair of electrons. It binds via two donor atoms to form a stable ring structure, acting as a didentate chelating ligand.

Step 4: Bonding mode of thiocyanate
Thiocyanate ion (\(\mathrm{SCN^{-}}\)) has two distinct potential donor atoms, namely sulfur and nitrogen (\(\mathrm{-SCN}\) or \(\mathrm{-NCS}\)), but binds through only one donor atom at a time to a given metal ion, making it an ambidentate unidentate ligand.

Step 5: Denticity of ammonia
Ammonia (\(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\)) is an uncharged molecule possessing a single lone pair of electrons on its nitrogen atom, functioning as a neutral unidentate ligand.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{EDTA^{4-}}\) matches hexadentate chelating ligand; ethane-1,2-diamine matches didentate chelating ligand; \(\mathrm{SCN^{-}}\) matches ambidentate unidentate ligand; and \(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\) matches neutral unidentate ligand.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q06 - Hybridisation and magnetic property of coordination entities

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions in Column I with their hybridisation and magnetic nature according to Valence Bond Theory in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\)i. \(sp^3\), paramagnetic
B. \(\mathrm{[CoF_{6}]^{3-}}\)ii. \(dsp^2\), diamagnetic
C. \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2-}}\)iii. \(sp^3d^2\), paramagnetic
D. \(\mathrm{[NiCl_{4}]^{2-}}\)iv. \(d^2sp^3\), diamagnetic

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Valence bond analysis of hexaamminecobalt(III)
Cobalt has an oxidation state of \(+3\) (\(3d^6\)). In the presence of \(\mathrm{NH_{3}}\), electron pairing occurs within the \(3d\) subshell, completely pairing all six electrons into three \(3d\) orbitals. Two empty \(3d\) orbitals along with one \(4s\) and three \(4p\) orbitals undergo \(d^2sp^3\) hybridisation. With zero unpaired electrons, the inner orbital complex is diamagnetic.

Step 2: Valence bond analysis of hexafluoridocobaltate(III)
Cobalt has an oxidation state of \(+3\) (\(3d^6\)). Fluoride is a weak field ligand and does not force pairing of the \(3d\) electrons, leaving four unpaired electrons. Hybridisation uses one \(4s\), three \(4p\), and two outer \(4d\) orbitals, producing \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation. The outer orbital complex is paramagnetic.

Step 3: Valence bond analysis of tetracyanidonickelate(II)
Nickel has an oxidation state of \(+2\) (\(3d^8\)). Cyanide is a strong field ligand that forces pairing of the two unpaired \(3d\) electrons into a single orbital, leaving one inner \(3d\) orbital vacant. This vacant \(3d\) orbital combines with the \(4s\) and two \(4p\) orbitals to undergo \(dsp^2\) hybridisation, yielding a square planar, diamagnetic complex.

Step 4: Valence bond analysis of tetrachloridonickelate(II)
Nickel has an oxidation state of \(+2\) (\(3d^8\)). Chloride is a weak field ligand and cannot cause electron pairing in the \(3d\) orbitals, leaving two unpaired electrons. The complex undergoes \(sp^3\) hybridisation involving one \(4s\) and three \(4p\) orbitals, forming a tetrahedral, paramagnetic complex.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) matches \(d^2sp^3\), diamagnetic; \(\mathrm{[CoF_{6}]^{3-}}\) matches \(sp^3d^2\), paramagnetic; \(\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2-}}\) matches \(dsp^2\), diamagnetic; and \(\mathrm{[NiCl_{4}]^{2-}}\) matches \(sp^3\), paramagnetic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q07 - Industrial and analytical applications of coordination entities

questiontext.text:
Match the reagent/complex in Column I with its specific application in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. Wilkinson catalyst, \(\mathrm{[(Ph_{3}P)_{3}RhCl]}\)i. Estimation of hardness of water
B. \(\mathrm{Na_{2}EDTA}\)ii. Extraction of gold and silver
C. Cyanide ion, \(\mathrm{CN^{-}}\)iii. Hydrogenation of alkenes
D. Sodium thiosulphate (Hypo)iv. Dissolving unreacted \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) in photography

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Industrial and laboratory roles of complexes
Coordination compounds find extensive application as catalysts, chelating reagents for analytical estimations, complexing agents in hydrometallurgical extractions, and fixing agents in photography.

Step 2: Role of Wilkinson catalyst
The rhodium complex chloridotris(triphenylphosphine)rhodium(I), known as Wilkinson catalyst \(\mathrm{[(Ph_{3}P)_{3}RhCl]}\), is used as a homogeneous catalyst for the hydrogenation of alkenes.

Step 3: Role of disodium EDTA
The disodium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (\(\mathrm{Na_{2}EDTA}\)) forms stable chelate complexes selectively with \(\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}\) and \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\) ions, enabling the precise estimation and volumetric titration of the hardness of water.

Step 4: Role of cyanide in extraction
In the extraction and metallurgy of noble metals like gold and silver, the crushed ore is leached in the presence of air using an aqueous cyanide solution, forming soluble coordination entities such as \(\mathrm{[Au(CN)_{2}]^{-}}\) and \(\mathrm{[Ag(CN)_{2}]^{-}}\).

Step 5: Role of hypo in black-and-white photography
During the fixing stage of photographic film processing, sodium thiosulphate solution acts as a complexing agent to dissolve unreacted, light-sensitive silver bromide by forming the soluble complex \(\mathrm{[Ag(S_{2}O_{3})_{2}]^{3-}}\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: Wilkinson catalyst matches hydrogenation of alkenes; \(\mathrm{Na_{2}EDTA}\) matches estimation of hardness of water; cyanide ion matches extraction of gold and silver; and sodium thiosulphate matches dissolving unreacted \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) in photography.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q08 - Absorbed and observed complementary colours in complexes

questiontext.text:
Match the coordination entities in Column I with the colour of light absorbed and their observed complementary colour in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}}\)i. Absorbs yellow light; observed colour is violet
B. \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+}}\)ii. Absorbs blue-green light; observed colour is purple / violet
C. \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+}}\)iii. Absorbs blue light; observed colour is yellow-orange
D. \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\)iv. Absorbs red light; observed colour is blue

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Crystal field theory and complementary colours
When white light falls on a transition metal complex, electrons are promoted from the \(t_{2g}\) level to the \(e_g\) level by absorbing radiation of a specific wavelength corresponding to the crystal field splitting energy (\(\Delta_o\)). The colour observed is the complementary colour of the light absorbed.

Step 2: Analysis of hexaaquatitanium(III)
In \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}}\), a \(d^1\) system, excitation of the single electron from the \(t_{2g}\) set to the \(e_g\) set corresponds to absorption of blue-green light (\(498\text{ nm}\)). The observed complementary colour of the complex is purple / violet.

Step 3: Analysis of tetraaquacopper(II)
In \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+}}\), the absorption occurs in the red wavelength region (\(600\text{ nm}\)), resulting in the characteristic observed blue colour of the solution.

Step 4: Analysis of pentaamminechloridocobalt(III)
In \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+}}\), substitution of an ammine ligand with a weaker-field chloride reduces \(\Delta_o\), shifting absorption to the yellow region (\(535\text{ nm}\)). Consequently, the complex transmits the complementary violet colour.

Step 5: Analysis of hexaamminecobalt(III)
In \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\), the presence of six strong-field ammine ligands produces a larger splitting \(\Delta_o\), causing the complex to absorb higher-energy blue light (\(475\text{ nm}\)). The complementary colour observed is yellow-orange.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Ti(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue-green and appears purple/violet; \(\mathrm{[Cu(H_{2}O)_{4}]^{2+}}\) absorbs red and appears blue; \(\mathrm{[CoCl(NH_{3})_{5}]^{2+}}\) absorbs yellow and appears violet; and \(\mathrm{[Co(NH_{3})_{6}]^{3+}}\) absorbs blue and appears yellow-orange.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q09 - Unpaired electrons and spin only magnetic moments

questiontext.text:
Match the complex ions in Column I with their number of unpaired electrons and spin-only magnetic moment (\(\mu_{\mathrm{s}}\)) in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\)i. \(5\text{ unpaired electrons, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 5.92\text{ BM}\)
B. \(\mathrm{[MnCl_{6}]^{3-}}\)ii. \(1\text{ unpaired electron, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 1.73\text{ BM}\)
C. \(\mathrm{[FeF_{6}]^{3-}}\)iii. \(2\text{ unpaired electrons, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 2.83\text{ BM}\)
D. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\)iv. \(4\text{ unpaired electrons, }\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = 4.90\text{ BM}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula for spin-only magnetic moment
The spin-only magnetic moment is given by \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{n(n+2)}\text{ BM}\), where \(n\) is the number of unpaired electrons in the complex entity.

Step 2: Electronic configuration of hexacyanidomanganate(III)
Manganese is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^4\) electronic configuration. Cyanide is a strong field ligand (\(\Delta_o > P\)), causing pairing in the \(t_{2g}\) set. The configuration is \(t_{2g}^4 e_g^0\), giving \(n = 2\) unpaired electrons. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83\text{ BM}\).

Step 3: Electronic configuration of hexachloridomanganate(III)
Manganese is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^4\) configuration. Chloride is a weak field ligand (\(\Delta_o < P\)), giving a high-spin distribution of \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^1\) with \(n = 4\) unpaired electrons. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\text{ BM}\).

Step 4: Electronic configuration of hexafluoridoferrate(III)
Iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^5\) configuration. Fluoride is a weak field ligand (\(\Delta_o < P\)), yielding a high-spin configuration of \(t_{2g}^3 e_g^2\) with \(n = 5\) unpaired electrons. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\text{ BM}\).

Step 5: Electronic configuration of hexacyanidoferrate(III)
Iron is in the \(+3\) oxidation state with a \(3d^5\) configuration. Cyanide is a strong field ligand (\(\Delta_o > P\)), driving complete pairing in the \(t_{2g}\) level to produce \(t_{2g}^5 e_g^0\), which contains \(n = 1\) unpaired electron. Its magnetic moment is \(\mu_{\mathrm{s}} = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73\text{ BM}\).

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Mn(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(2\) unpaired electrons (\(2.83\text{ BM}\)); \(\mathrm{[MnCl_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(4\) unpaired electrons (\(4.90\text{ BM}\)); \(\mathrm{[FeF_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(5\) unpaired electrons (\(5.92\text{ BM}\)); and \(\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_{6}]^{3-}}\) has \(1\) unpaired electron (\(1.73\text{ BM}\)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_COORDINATION_COMPOUNDS_MATCH_Q10 - Metal carbonyl structures and oxidation states

questiontext.text:
Match the homoleptic metal carbonyls in Column I with their structural description and features in Column II:

Column IColumn II
A. \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\)i. Octahedral geometry with central metal in zero oxidation state
B. \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\)ii. Two square pyramidal units joined by a metal-metal bond
C. \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_{6}]}\)iii. Tetrahedral geometry with central metal in zero oxidation state
D. \(\mathrm{[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]}\)iv. Trigonal bipyramidal geometry with central metal in zero oxidation state

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of metal carbonyl structures and bonding
Homoleptic metal carbonyls are complexes containing only carbon monoxide ligands coordinated to transition metals in zero oxidation states. The metal-carbon bond possesses both \(\sigma\) donation from carbonyl carbon to metal and \(\pi\) back-bonding from filled metal \(d\) orbitals to empty \(\pi^*\) orbitals of \(\mathrm{CO}\).

Step 2: Analysis of tetracarbonylnickel(0)
Tetracarbonylnickel(0), \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\), has a nickel atom in the zero oxidation state surrounded symmetrically by four carbonyl ligands in a tetrahedral geometry.

Step 3: Analysis of pentacarbonyliron(0)
Pentacarbonyliron(0), \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\), contains iron in the zero oxidation state coordinated to five carbonyl groups positioned at the vertices of a trigonal bipyramid.

Step 4: Analysis of hexacarbonylchromium(0)
Hexacarbonylchromium(0), \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_{6}]}\), features a chromium atom in the zero oxidation state coordinated to six carbonyl groups arranged in an octahedral geometry.

Step 5: Analysis of decacarbonyldimanganese(0)
Decacarbonyldimanganese(0), \(\mathrm{[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]}\), is a dinuclear neutral carbonyl composed of two square pyramidal \(\mathrm{Mn(CO)_{5}}\) units joined together by a single manganese-manganese (\(\mathrm{Mn-Mn}\)) covalent bond without any bridging carbonyl groups.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
The correct correspondence is: \(\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_{4}]}\) has a tetrahedral geometry with zero oxidation state; \(\mathrm{[Fe(CO)_{5}]}\) has a trigonal bipyramidal geometry with zero oxidation state; \(\mathrm{[Cr(CO)_{6}]}\) has an octahedral geometry with zero oxidation state; and \(\mathrm{[Mn_{2}(CO)_{10}]}\) consists of two square pyramidal units joined by a metal-metal bond.
